caption: A magnet is held against a plastic toy and released, and the magnet falls to the floor.

sa.check: A magnet is held against the toy.
The magnet is released: the hand lets go.
The magnet falls to the floor.
The toy looks like moulded plastic.
The order is hold, release, fall.

pc.expect: The instant the hand opens, the magnet leaves the plastic surface and begins to fall.
pc.fail: The magnet stays on the plastic after release with nothing supporting it; or creeps down the toy's surface still in contact with it; or hangs at a gap from the toy; or the toy lifts away with the magnet.

pc.expect: The magnet falls straight down from where it was let go and comes to rest on the floor below.
pc.fail: The magnet drifts upward or sideways after release; or halts in mid-air; or lands and then rises back up to the toy.

pc.expect: The toy stays put as the magnet is released and falls; once landed the magnet lies still.
pc.fail: The toy tips, slides or lifts as the magnet drops; or the landed magnet slides toward the toy with nothing pushing it; or the magnet starts moving again after coming to rest.

pc.expect: The toy and the magnet keep their shapes; the floor stays flat where the magnet lands.
pc.fail: The toy stays dented after the magnet has left it; or the magnet squashes or flattens on landing; or the floor dents under the magnet.

pc.expect: One magnet and one toy; the magnet passes through neither the toy nor the floor and does not vanish on the way down.
pc.fail: The magnet vanishes in mid-fall; or a second magnet appears; or the magnet passes into the toy or through the floor; or the toy turns into another object.

pc.expect: The toy's colours, the magnet's colour and shape and the floor stay the same.
pc.fail: The toy changes colour; or the magnet changes shape or colour between release and landing; or the floor pattern changes.

note: P1 assumes the toy shown is plastic, as the caption says. A toy that plainly reads as metal fails S1 and S5; the magnet holding on such a toy is then not a P1 failure.
